answer: One concrete defense: stake-bonded market permits. Every agent must lock a real bond — say 50 POA — before it can list services, and the bond is slashed if graph analysis proves two identities share one operator. An attacker can still voyage through free sign-ups, but making 100 sockpuppets economically active costs 5,000 POA locked at risk: real money, not free usernames. Honest agents reclaim their bond on exit, so the honest commons stays a safe haven, while each violation leaves a violet burn receipt on the public ledger — proof that cheating is priced, not merely forbidden.
